### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Root problem (the only one the customer named): end the dental rider at her own request.**

*Hub:* `member_ending_a_rider_on_the_call_5d09e2f1.json`, "Ending an Optional Supplemental Benefit
Rider at the Member's Own Request", section "The condition the closing figure waits on".

**Edge A — state form — STATE-DERIVED.**
Sentence, verbatim: "The rider premium left owed when a rider is closed is fixed only once the
rider stands suspended for unpaid premium on its own record."
Records: `find_osb_riders` → `status 'active'`. The state named does not hold. The sentence names
a *state* and no action. Searching the corpus with the words the record and the sentence use —
"suspended for unpaid premium", "rider premium" — reaches
*Recording a Rider as Suspended for Unpaid Premium* ("The rider is put into premium suspension and
the rider premium the member owes is restated to the arrears figure given … The member's rider
record shows the rider suspended for unpaid premium") and *Suspension of a Rider for Unpaid
Premium and its Recovery*, which states when a suspension is due. That is the write that brings
the waited-on state about, and the records show it is due: the 2026-06 charge has stood part-paid
since 2026-06-01 and the rider's 60 days of grace, counted from 2026-06-02, ran out on 2026-07-31.
→ **Problem 2: record the rider as suspended for unpaid premium.**

**Edge B — state form — STATE-DERIVED.**
*Hub:* `recording_suspension_for_unpaid_rider_premium_9ad34f78.json`, section "The condition the
figure waits on". Sentence, verbatim: "The rider premium standing owed is not struck until every
billing cycle the rider has been in force through carries a rider premium charge on the rider
premium account."
Records: the rider has been in force since `rider_effective_date '2026-03-01'`; a billing cycle
carries three coverage months (*Coverage Months a Billing Cycle Carries on a Rider Premium
Charge*, the enrollment standing in force and billed quarterly), so the cycles run March–May,
June–August and September–November. The ledger carries charges booked to `2026-03` and `2026-06`
and none for the cycle beginning `2026-09`. The state does not hold.
Searching with the records' words — "rider premium charge", "premium account", "coverage the plan
has not yet billed" — reaches *Raising a Rider Premium Charge on the Premium Account* ("the plan
raises the rider premium owed and posts it to that rider's premium account, booked to the
coverage month named") and *Striking the Rider Premium Raised for Coverage Not Yet Billed*. That
is the write.
→ **Problem 3: raise the rider premium for the coverage months not yet billed.**

No further edge: *Raising a Rider Premium Charge on the Premium Account* carries no
"condition … waits on" section, and nothing in the records contradicts that.

**Resulting tree and handling order.**

```
   Problem 3  raise the premium for coverage not yet billed   (agent)
        │
        ▼
   Problem 2  record the rider as suspended for unpaid premium (agent)
        │
        ▼
   Problem 1  end the rider at the member's own request        (user)   ← the only one the customer named
```

Order: 3 → 2 → 1, strictly. The caller mentions neither of the first two and could not: "You have
no idea what is or is not sitting on your account, you have never been told anything was wrong
with it, and you would not know one kind of charge from another."

**Hop marks.** Edge A: state-derived. Edge B: state-derived. **No hop is pre-solved.** The
corpus-wide check recorded in task 0's blind answer applies here: exactly seven documents name a

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every quantity above is read from a quoted sentence of a
published document plus a finder return.

**The closest alternatives, and the visible sentence that excludes each.**

| Closest alternative | Excluded by |
|---|---|
| End the rider on the day the form was received (2026-09-14) or on today's date | *Cancellation, Minimum Holding and Reinstatement Terms*: the end date is "the last day of the month in which the request was received" — 2026-09-30. The persona expressly refuses to guess: "you would rather they told you what the proper date is" |
| Refuse the cancellation as inside the minimum holding period | Same schedule: 6 months on the Ridgecrest Comprehensive Dental Rider, effective 2026-03-01, request received 2026-09-14 |
| Raise one coverage month's premium (28.60) rather than a cycle's | *Counting the Coverage Months Not Yet Billed on a Rider* case 1 takes "a whole cycle's worth", and *Coverage Months a Billing Cycle Carries…* puts the cycle at three on an enrollment in force and billed quarterly |
| Raise premium for every month back to the rider effective date (7 months) | The same case 1 governs, the account already carrying a charge and the record carrying no day the rider ended; the "whole calendar months from the day the rider took effect" reading belongs to the case where the account carries no charge at all |
| Book the new charge to `2026-10` or to `2026-11` | *Raising a Rider Premium Charge…*: "Where a charge covers several coverage months it is booked to the earliest of them"; the unbilled cycle begins in September |
| Strike the arrears over the rider's own 60 days of grace | *Which Days of Grace Govern the Span…* case 1: the plan's 90 days are more than the rider's 60, so the plan's govern. Had the rider's 60 governed, the credit of 12.40 posted 2026-07-05 would have fallen outside the span and the figure would have been 85.80 — so the tier is not decorative |
| Take the figure the rider record shows standing owed | *Which Arrears Figure is Taken…* case 1: the rider stands at active and the two figures differ, so the entries struck give the figure |
| Strike every entry on the account into the arrears | *Which Rider Premium Charges are Struck at Suspension* / *…Payments…* / *…Credits…* all put an active rider with no day it ended on the within-the-span case; "every entry" belongs to the other standings |
| Compute the closing figure from the ledger rather than the record | *What Stands Owed on a Rider at the Moment of Closure* case 1: the rider now stands suspended for unpaid premium, so "what stands owed is the figure the rider record shows standing owed" |
| Refund three coverage months, or none | *Counting the Coverage Months Falling Beyond the Day a Rider Ends* case 1: the cycle's three less the month the intake reached the plan less no further whole month = 2 |
| Refund at 85.80 a month | *The Rate a Coverage Month is Refunded At on Closure* case 1: the largest charge carries more than one coverage month, so the amount is divided by them |
| Set nothing from the medical plan bill against the closing figure | *Money on the Medical Plan Bill Set Against a Closing Rider Figure* case 2: the bill carries money received (the 147.60 posted 2026-09-04 marked `overpayment`) and 4.80 stands left over |
| Have the representative end the rider | The tool's own document: "The tool belongs to the member: the representative unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to end the rider they are paying for"; and the persona: "You will press the button yourself" |
| End the medical plan as well | *How an Optional Supplemental Benefit Rider Comes to an End* §6: "Ending a rider does not end the allowance card or the medical plan"; the tool doc: "The member's medical plan, their allowance card and any other rider are untouched"; and the persona: "certainly not" |

**Boundaries the source leaves open are left open.** No document says whether the cancellation
intake's own `requested_effective_date` overrides the schedule's rule; none is needed here,
because the two agree (both 2026-09-30), and I derived the date from the rule rather than the
field. I record the coincidence rather than relying on it.

**Counter-proof against the natural wrong answer — "she asked only that the rider be ended, so
end it".** Doing only that leaves the governed result in a state the visible principles forbid:
*Ending an Optional Supplemental Benefit Rider at the Member's Own Request* states that "The rider
premium left owed when a rider is closed is fixed only once the rider stands suspended for unpaid
premium on its own record", and `find_osb_riders` returns `status 'active'`. The closing figure
is a required parameter of the ending itself, so there is no reading on which the rider can be
ended now and the figure settled later. And the suspension in turn cannot strike its figure while
*Recording a Rider as Suspended for Unpaid Premium* states that "The rider premium standing owed
is not struck until every billing cycle the rider has been in force through carries a rider
premium charge on the rider premium account" and the September cycle carries none.

That both edges bear weight on the scored number is visible: ending the rider on the record's own
46.40 would give a closing figure nowhere near 11.40, and suspending without first raising the
September charge would strike 0.00 − 12.40 → nothing at all, since no charge would fall inside the
governing span.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.** Reading only each computation
document and the product figures it names, with no factor applied:

| Computation | Fall-back (baseline only) | Answer reached |
|---|---|---|
| Rider premium raised for coverage not yet billed | one charge carries 1 coverage month; not yet billed = 2026-03-01 → 2026-09-21 counting the month of effect = 7; the most one charge may carry = 2026-09-01 → 2026-09-21 = 0; already met = the number of payments posted = 1; months charged = min(7, 0) − 1, never fewer than none = 0 → **0.00** | 85.80 |
| Rider premium standing owed at suspension | §5 governs: "The figure taken is the one the rider record shows standing owed" → **132.20** (46.40 before the charge in (a), 132.20 after it); the §1 entries reading gives 257.40 − 85.80 − 30.80 = 140.80 | 73.40 |
| Rider premium left owed at closure | a billing cycle carries 1 coverage month; what stands owed = every charge less every payment and credit = 140.80; no coverage month falls beyond the end so the refund is nothing; nothing is set against it from the plan bill → **140.80** | 11.40 |

Each is computable and definite from its own document plus the schedules it names, and each
differs from the answer reached. No computation document hints that a variation exists.

Every one was reached from the records' own vocabulary, not from the computation document's
wording and not by guessing that a variation exists.

### Observation carried forward to the scan (not a conclusion)

Three documents state a rule for a coverage-month count on a rider premium charge:
*Coverage Months a Billing Cycle Carries on a Rider Premium Charge*, *Coverage Months Carried by
a Single Rider Premium Charge* and *Length of a Billing Cycle When a Rider is Closed*. Their
third tiers differ in their anchor — "the day the rider took effect" against "the day the plan
received the rider request" — so they are not restatements of one another. Their titles do
distinguish the quantity each settles, and on both tasks' worlds the enrollment stands in force
and is billed quarterly, so all three give 3 and no number turns on telling them apart. Recorded
here so the two-way scan can check that each belongs to a distinct declared factor.

### contamination_disclosure

None. The only task JSON fields read before this freeze were `user_scenario` and `frozen_time`,
each extracted by an explicit single-key print, never by grep. No `tasks/*.json` path entered any
search domain. The brief's two renderer leads carried no scored value, no gold parameter and no
intermediate, and no figure above was taken from them.

### Verdict

**PASS** — no `KB-RUNTIME RED`.

From the published documents and tool-shaped queries alone, the three-problem chain, its
direction, its strict order and all three scored values were derived and equal the source
layer's. No hop was pre-solved; no conclusion required hidden compute, GT or the raw
`initial_state`.

Noted, not a finding: the accepted base defect concerning
`osb_premium_suspension_and_recovery`'s `rider_grace_period_exhausted` surfaces here as
`suspend_rider_for_unpaid_premium_a0d6b513`'s `osb_rider_premium_entry_id`, which no
computation reads. It did not obstruct this derivation: the KB describes it as "the reference
number of the earliest rider premium charge that went unpaid on that rider, read from the
member's rider premium account entries", and the ledger makes `f540db99-…` the unique answer,
which is the value the source carries.

### Observation from the blind answer, now resolved

The blind answer flagged that three documents state a coverage-month rule for a rider premium
charge. The source confirms they are three distinct declared factors of three distinct
computations — `plan_bill_cycle_months` of `osb_ext_precover_premium_credit`
(*Coverage Months Carried by a Single Rider Premium Charge*), `plan_bill_cycle_length` of
`osb_ext_unbilled_cycle_premium_charge` (*Coverage Months a Billing Cycle Carries on a Rider
Premium Charge*) and `billing_cycle_length` of `osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement`
(*Length of a Billing Cycle When a Rider is Closed*) — and the blind audit assigned each to the
right computation. Not a finding.
